title: Multiplying and Dividing Decimal Fractions
seo_title: Grade 6 Multiplying and Dividing Decimals Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Multiply decimal fractions by 10 and 100; divide decimal fractions by 10 and 100; multiply and divide decimal fractions by whole numbers; solve problems in context involving decimal fractions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 worksheets: multiplying and dividing decimals by 10, 100 and 1 000 and by whole numbers, estimating and problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: × 10: digits move left. ÷ 10: digits move right.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • × 10 moves every digit one place to the left; ÷ 10 moves every digit one place to the right.
  • 3,45 × 100 = 345; 3,45 ÷ 10 = 0,345.
  • Decimal × whole number: multiply as whole numbers, then put in the comma. 2,3 × 4: 23 × 4 = 92, so 9,2.
  • Estimate to check where the comma goes.

Examples

Example

4,8 ÷ 6

48 ÷ 6 = 8 tenths

Answer: 0,8

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding a 03,45 × 10 = 34,5, not 3,450.
The comma in the wrong placeEstimate: 2,3 × 4 is about 8.
No commaCount the decimal places.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about multiplying decimals?
faq.a: Multiply and divide decimal fractions by 10 and 100, and multiply and divide decimal fractions by whole numbers.

items.q: The chart shows 2,4 × 10. What is the answer?
items.e: 2,4 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. 2,4 × 10 = 24. 2,40 is wrong: adding a zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value.

items.q: The chart shows 3,6 ÷ 10. What is the answer?
items.e: 3,6 ÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 3,6 ÷ 10 = 0,36. 36 moves the digits the wrong way.

items.q: Which calculation does the chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 1 place to the left, so the number was multiplied by 10. 3,27 × 10 = 32,7.

items.q: Which calculation does the chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 2 places to the right, so the number was divided by 100. 58,4 ÷ 100 = 0,584.

items.q: In 6,2 × 1 000, how do the digits move?
items.e: 1 000 has 3 zeros, so every digit moves 3 places. Multiplying makes the number bigger, so they move to the left: 6,2 × 1 000 = 6 200.

items.q: The chart shows 0,046 × 100 = 4,6. What is the value of the red digit in the answer?
items.e: The 6 was in the thousandths place. Every digit moved 2 places to the left, so the 6 is now in the tenths place. Its value is 6 tenths = 0,6.

items.q: The chart shows 7,31 ÷ 10 = 0,731. What is the value of the red digit in the answer?
items.e: The 3 was in the tenths place. Every digit moved 1 place to the right, so the 3 is now in the hundredths place. Its value is 3 hundredths = 0,03.
12,05 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. 12,05 × 10 = 120,5. 120,05 only multiplies the whole number part. Every digit must move, including the 5.
260 ÷ 1 000: every digit moves 3 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 260 ÷ 1 000 = 0,26. The last 0 is not needed after the point.
The 9 moves from the tenths to the tens: that is 2 places to the left, so the missing number is 100. 89,1 is 90 − 0,9, which is subtraction, not multiplication.
0,37 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0,37 × 10 = 3,7.
0,4 ÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 0,4 ÷ 10 = 0,04.
0,008 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0,008 × 100 = 0,8.
309 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. 309 ÷ 100 = 3,09.
The 4 moved from the ones to the thousands: that is 3 places to the left, so the number is 1 000. (4,5 × 100 = 450.)
The 1 moved from the tens to the hundredths: that is 3 places to the right, so it is ÷ 1 000. (18 ÷ 100 = 0,18.)

items.q: Which calculation has the answer 0,63?
The chart shows 70,5 ÷ 100 = 0,705. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 70,5 ÷ 100 = 0,705. Every digit moved 2 places to the right, so the 5 is now in the thousandths place. Its value is 5 thousandths.

items.q: The chart shows 3,42 × 10 = 34,2. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 3,42 × 10 = 34,2. Every digit moved 1 place to the left, so the 4 is now in the ones place. Its value is 4 ones.

items.q: The chart shows 86 ÷ 1 000 = 0,086. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 86 ÷ 1 000 = 0,086. Every digit moved 3 places to the right, so the 8 is now in the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths.

items.q: The number line shows 4 jumps of 0,3. What is 4 × 0,3?
items.e: 0,3 is 3 tenths. 4 × 3 = 12, so 4 × 0,3 = 12 tenths = 1,2. The red dot is 2 small ticks past 1, at 1,2. 4,3 adds the numbers instead of multiplying.

items.q: The number line shows 6 jumps of 0,4. What is 6 × 0,4?
items.e: 0,4 is 4 tenths. 6 × 4 = 24, so 6 × 0,4 = 24 tenths = 2,4. The red dot is 4 small ticks past 2, at 2,4.
0,2 is 2 tenths. 6 × 2 = 12, so 6 × 0,2 = 12 tenths = 1,2. 12 forgets that 0,2 is only 2 tenths.
0,5 is 5 tenths. 7 × 5 = 35, so 7 × 0,5 = 35 tenths = 3,5. 0,35 puts the decimal point one place too far left.

items.q: 8 × 0,3 means 8 groups of 3 tenths, which is 24 tenths. What is 24 tenths as a decimal?
items.e: 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 24 tenths = 2 wholes and 4 tenths = 2,4. 0,24 is 24 hundredths.
0,3 is 3 tenths. 24 × 3 = 72, so 24 × 0,3 = 72 tenths = 7,2. 72 forgets to divide by 10. 8 is 24 ÷ 3: you multiply here, you do not divide.
0,6 is 6 tenths. 15 × 6 = 90, so 15 × 0,6 = 90 tenths = 9. 90 forgets that 0,6 is less than 1, so the answer must be less than 15.
0,7 is 7 tenths. 9 × 7 = 63, so 9 × 0,7 = 63 tenths = 6,3. You can multiply in any order: 0,7 × 9 = 9 × 0,7.
0,2 is 2 tenths. 45 × 2 = 90, so 45 × 0,2 = 90 tenths = 9. 45,2 adds 0,2 to 45 instead of multiplying.
0,4 is 4 tenths. 32 × 4 = 128, so 32 × 0,4 = 128 tenths = 12,8. 8 is 32 ÷ 4. 128 forgets to divide by 10.
3 tenths × 4 = 12 tenths. 10 tenths make 1 one, so 12 tenths = 1,2.
6 tenths × 5 = 30 tenths. 10 tenths make 1 one, so 30 tenths = 3.
8 hundredths × 7 = 56 hundredths = 0,56.
4 hundredths × 3 = 12 hundredths. 10 hundredths make 1 tenth, so the answer is 0,12.
Tenths: 4 × 3 = 12. Write 2, exchange 1 one. Ones: 1 × 3 + 1 = 4. Write 4. The point goes straight below the point: 4,2.
Tenths: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 ones. Ones: 2 × 4 + 2 = 10. Write 10. The point goes straight below the point: 10,4.
Tenths: 7 × 6 = 42. Write 2, exchange 4 ones. Ones: 3 × 6 + 4 = 22. Write 22. The point goes straight below the point: 22,2.
Tenths: 8 × 7 = 56. Write 6, exchange 5 ones. Ones: 5 × 7 + 5 = 40. Write 40. The point goes straight below the point: 40,6.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 2,45 × 6?
items.e: Hundredths: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3 tenths. Tenths: 4 × 6 + 3 = 27. Write 7, exchange 2 ones. Ones: 2 × 6 + 2 = 14. Write 14. The point goes straight below the point: 14,70 = 14,7.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 1,36 × 4?
items.e: Hundredths: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tenths. Tenths: 3 × 4 + 2 = 14. Write 4, exchange 1 one. Ones: 1 × 4 + 1 = 5. Write 5. The point goes straight below the point: 5,44.
0,8 is 8 tenths. 8 ÷ 2 = 4, so 0,8 ÷ 2 = 4 tenths = 0,4. Check: 0,4 × 2 = 0,8. 1,6 multiplies instead of dividing.
2,4 is 24 tenths. 24 ÷ 6 = 4, so 2,4 ÷ 6 = 4 tenths = 0,4. Check: 0,4 × 6 = 2,4. 2,5 is 6 ÷ 2,4: it divides the wrong way round.
6,3 is 63 tenths. 63 ÷ 3 = 21, so 6,3 ÷ 3 = 21 tenths = 2,1. Check: 2,1 × 3 = 6,3. 2,3 divides only the 6 and forgets the 3 tenths.
8,4 is 84 tenths. 84 ÷ 4 = 21, so 8,4 ÷ 4 = 21 tenths = 2,1. Check: 2,1 × 4 = 8,4. 2,4 divides only the 8 and forgets the 4 tenths.
5,6 is 56 tenths. 56 ÷ 8 = 7, so 5,6 ÷ 8 = 7 tenths = 0,7. Check: 0,7 × 8 = 5,6. 5,6 is less than 8, so the answer is less than 1. 44,8 multiplies.
4,56 is 456 hundredths. 456 ÷ 4 = 114, so 4,56 ÷ 4 = 114 hundredths = 1,14. Check: 1,14 × 4 = 4,56. 1,56 divides only the 4 ones. 11,4 puts the point in the wrong place.

items.q: 4,56 is 456 hundredths. What is 456 hundredths ÷ 4?
items.e: 456 ÷ 4 = 114, and the unit stays the same: 114 hundredths = 1,14. So 4,56 ÷ 4 = 1,14.
7,25 is 725 hundredths. 725 ÷ 5 = 145, so 7,25 ÷ 5 = 145 hundredths = 1,45. Check: 1,45 × 5 = 7,25. 14,5 is 10 times too big: 7,25 ÷ 5 must be less than 2.
9,36 is 936 hundredths. 936 ÷ 3 = 312, so 9,36 ÷ 3 = 312 hundredths = 3,12. Check: 3,12 × 3 = 9,36. 3,36 divides only the 9 ones.

items.q: The quotient digits for 7,38 ÷ 3 are 2, 4, 6. Where does the decimal point go?
items.e: Put the decimal point in the quotient straight above the point in 7,38. Estimate: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so the answer is between 2 and 3. 7,38 ÷ 3 = 2,46.

items.q: Use short division. What is 8,4 ÷ 4?
items.e: 8 ÷ 4 = 2; 4 ÷ 4 = 1. Keep the point in line: 8,4 ÷ 4 = 2,1.

items.q: Use short division. What is 9,36 ÷ 3?
Use short division. What is 7,38 ÷ 6?
Use short division. What is 4,08 ÷ 4?
17 ÷ 4 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 17 as 17,00 (the grey zeros). 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1. Exchange the 1 for 10 tenths: 10 ÷ 4 = 2 r 2. Exchange the 2 tenths for 20 hundredths: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Answer: 4,25. (4,1 writes the remainder 1 as a decimal, but r 1 means 1 left over out of 4, which is 0,25.)
2 ÷ 8 = 0 r 2; 24 ÷ 8 = 3. Keep the point in line: 2,4 ÷ 8 = 0,3.

items.q: 13 ÷ 5 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 13 as 13,0 so you can keep dividing. 13 ÷ 5 = 2 r 3; 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Keep the point in line: 13 ÷ 5 = 2,6. (Not 2,3: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: 23 ÷ 4 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 23 as 23,00 so you can keep dividing. 23 ÷ 4 = 5 r 3; 30 ÷ 4 = 7 r 2; 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Keep the point in line: 23 ÷ 4 = 5,75. (Not 5,3: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 6,9 × 4?
items.e: 6,9 is close to 7, and 7 × 4 = 28. (Exactly: 27,6.) 24 rounds 6,9 down to 6, but 6,9 is much closer to 7.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 19,8 ÷ 5?
items.e: 19,8 is close to 20, and 20 ÷ 5 = 4. (Exactly: 3,96.) 99 is 19,8 × 5: it multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 3,1 × 9?
items.e: 3,1 is close to 3, and 3 × 9 = 27. (Exactly: 27,9.) 36 rounds 3,1 up to 4.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 0,48 × 30?
items.e: 0,48 is close to 0,5, which is one half. Half of 30 is 15. (Exactly: 14,4.) 12 uses 0,4, but 0,48 is much closer to 0,5.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 61,2 ÷ 3?
items.e: 61,2 is close to 60, and 60 ÷ 3 = 20. (Exactly: 20,4.) 180 is about 61,2 × 3: it multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: The digits of 3,8 × 7 are 266. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 3,8 × 7?
items.e: Estimate: 4 × 7 = 28, so the answer is close to 28. So 3,8 × 7 = 26,6.

items.q: The digits of 41,6 ÷ 8 are 52. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 41,6 ÷ 8?
items.e: Estimate: 40 ÷ 8 = 5, so the answer is close to 5. So 41,6 ÷ 8 = 5,2.

items.q: Use an estimate to choose the correct answer to 48,6 ÷ 6.
items.e: 48,6 is close to 48, and 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Only 8,1 is close to 8. Check: 8,1 × 6 = 48,6.

items.q: The digits of 5,25 × 4 are 2 100. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 5,25 × 4?
items.e: Estimate: 5 × 4 = 20, so the answer is close to 20. The digits 2 100 mean 21,00, which is 21. So 5,25 × 4 = 21.

items.q: The digits of 9,45 ÷ 7 are 135. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 9,45 ÷ 7?
items.e: Estimate: 7 ÷ 7 = 1 and 14 ÷ 7 = 2, so the answer is between 1 and 2. So 9,45 ÷ 7 = 1,35.

items.q: Ofentse says 4,8 × 10 = 4,80. Is she right?
items.e: 4,80 has the same value as 4,8, so adding a zero did not multiply. Estimate: 5 × 10 = 50. The digits move 1 place to the left: 4,8 × 10 = 48.

items.q: Sibusiso says 36,5 ÷ 100 = 3 650. What did he do wrong?
c: He forgot to add a zero
He moved the digits the wrong way
He moved the digits too few places
items.e: Dividing makes the number smaller, but 3 650 is bigger than 36,5. He moved the digits the wrong way. 36,5 ÷ 100 = 0,365.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 3,9 × 20?
items.e: Round 3,9 to 4. 4 × 20 = 80. 60 rounds 3,9 down to 3, but 3,9 is much closer to 4.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 6,1 × 300?
Which is the best estimate for 0,48 × 50?
items.e: Round 0,48 to 0,5. 0,5 × 50 = 25 (half of 50). 20 uses 0,4, but 0,48 is closer to 0,5.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 59,7 ÷ 20?
items.e: Round 59,7 to 60. 60 ÷ 20 = 3. 1 200 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 8,1 ÷ 40?
5,06 × 1 000 is closest to which number?
0,38 ÷ 10 is closest to which number?
Use an estimate to choose the correct answer: 2,9 × 40 = ?
items.e: Estimate: 3 × 40 = 120. Only 116 is close to the estimate. The other answers have the digits in the wrong places.

items.q: A 2,25 ℓ bottle of juice is shared equally among 5 friends. How much juice does each friend get?
items.e: 2,25 ℓ is 225 hundredths. 225 ÷ 5 = 45, so each friend gets 45 hundredths = 0,45 ℓ (450 mℓ). 11,25 ℓ multiplies: each friend cannot get more than the whole bottle.

items.q: Priya runs 0,8 km every day for 15 days. How far does she run in all?
items.e: 15 × 0,8 = 15 × 8 tenths = 120 tenths = 12 km. 120 km forgets to divide by 10. 15,8 km adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: Each batch of pancakes uses 0,3 ℓ of milk. How much milk is needed for 14 batches?
items.e: 14 × 0,3 = 14 × 3 tenths = 42 tenths = 4,2 ℓ. 42 ℓ forgets to divide by 10.

items.q: Sarah cuts a 4,5 m ribbon into 9 equal pieces for the class banner. How long is each piece?
items.e: 4,5 is 45 tenths. 45 ÷ 9 = 5, so each piece is 5 tenths = 0,5 m (50 cm). 2 m is 9 ÷ 4,5: it divides the wrong way round.

items.q: A 3 ℓ jug of water fills paper cups that hold 0,2 ℓ each. How many cups can be filled?
items.e: 3 ÷ 0,2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cups. Each litre fills 5 cups. 0,6 is 3 × 0,2: it multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A 7,2 km hiking trail is split into 8 equal sections. How long is each section?
items.e: 7,2 is 72 tenths. 72 ÷ 8 = 9, so each section is 9 tenths = 0,9 km. 9 km is longer than the whole trail.

items.q: On a canoe trip, 9 campers share a 1,35 kg bag of trail mix equally. How much does each camper get?
items.e: 1,35 is 135 hundredths. 135 ÷ 9 = 15, so each camper gets 15 hundredths = 0,15 kg (150 g). 1,5 kg is more than the whole bag.

items.q: Megan’s dog eats 0,4 kg of food a day. How many days does a 12 kg bag last?
A cedar board 3,6 m long is cut into 4 equal pieces for a garden box. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3,6 is 36 tenths. 36 ÷ 4 = 9, so each piece is 9 tenths = 0,9 m (90 cm). 9 m is longer than the whole board.

items.q: A bag of rice has a mass of 2,5 kg. How many grams is that? (1 kg = 1 000 g)
items.e: Multiply by 1 000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. 2,5 × 1 000 = 2 500 g. 250 g multiplies by 100 only.

items.q: Ravi’s dog eats 0,35 kg of food every day. How much food does it eat in one week?
items.e: One week is 7 days. 0,35 × 7 = 35 hundredths × 7 = 245 hundredths = 2,45 kg. 7,35 kg adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: A 2,4 ℓ jug of orange juice is poured equally into 8 cups. How many millilitres are in each cup?
items.e: 2,4 ÷ 8 = 24 tenths ÷ 8 = 3 tenths = 0,3 ℓ. 1 ℓ = 1 000 mℓ, so 0,3 × 1 000 = 300 mℓ. 30 mℓ multiplies by 100 instead of 1 000.

items.q: Karabo’s family cycles 9,6 km around the Stanley Park seawall. They split the ride into 4 equal parts. How long is each part?
items.e: 9,6 is 96 tenths. 96 ÷ 4 = 24, so each part is 24 tenths = 2,4 km. Estimate: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. 38,4 km multiplies by 4.

items.q: Daniel pours 3 bottles of water, each 1,75 ℓ, into a cooler for his lacrosse team. The water is shared equally among 5 players. How much water does each player get?
items.e: Total: 1,75 × 3 = 5,25 ℓ. Each player: 5,25 ÷ 5 = 525 hundredths ÷ 5 = 105 hundredths = 1,05 ℓ. 1,5 ℓ drops the 0 that holds the tenths place. 5,25 ℓ is the total, not each player’s share.

items.q: Kgomotso cuts a 3,6 m ribbon into 8 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3,6 ÷ 8: 8 does not go into 3, so write 0. 36 tenths ÷ 8 = 4 r 4. Exchange the 4 tenths for 40 hundredths: 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Each piece is 0,45 m (45 cm). (0,44 m writes the remainder 4 as the next digit.)

items.q: A bag of apples has a mass of 1,25 kg. What is the mass of 6 bags?
items.e: 1,25 × 6. Hundredths: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3 tenths. Tenths: 2 × 6 + 3 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1 one. Ones: 1 × 6 + 1 = 7. Write 7. Keep the point in line: 7,50 kg. The 6 bags have a mass of 7,5 kg.

items.q: In the long jump, Ravi jumps 3,2 m and Thandi jumps 2,85 m. How much further does Ravi jump?
Daniel cuts 8 m of rope into 3 equal pieces. How long is each piece, to 1 decimal place?
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2,66… To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit: 6, so round up. Each piece is 2,7 m. (2,2 m writes the remainder 2 as a decimal.)

items.q: A sunflower grows from 0,85 m to 1,6 m tall. How much does it grow?
One lap of the school field is 0,4 km. Anika runs 7 laps. How far does she run?
items.e: 4 tenths × 7 = 28 tenths = 2,8 km.
